title: Embedding Adapter: Cursor Translation & Error Semantics for Legacy SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
scope: In scope: gateway-side translation for /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank iterator endpoints, mapping cursor token formats, reverse-mapping tombstone semantics, and error code normalization. Out of scope: changing customer SDKs, reworking offline vector stores, or changing underlying model ranking logic.
approach_and_design:
High level approach: implement an adapter middleware that performs three tasks: (A) Cursor translation: accept both legacy opaque cursors and new tokens, normalize to a stable internal representation, and emit legacy-style tokens to legacy clients. We will implement a stable token namespace (prefix 'lc:' + base64(payload) + HMAC) so tokens are verifiable without coupling to internal JSON shapes. (B) Tombstone handling: when the new API returns tombstoned ids, the adapter will surface them as empty results plus a stable cursor that skips tombstones for forward iteration; optional 'include_tombstones' query param will be honored for advanced clients. (C) Error mapping: convert fine-grained RPC errors to legacy HTTP codes expected by older clients, and add Retry-After/Idempotency-Token headers where beneficial. Example mappings (adapter behavior): rate_limit -> 429 (propagate Retry-After); transient_kv_failure -> 503; partial_consistency -> 206 with X-Partial-Results; validation_error -> 400. We will publish the exact mapping in the migration doc.

Trade-offs: doing translation at gateway adds latency (~5–12ms median) on affected calls. Alternate approach would be client SDK patches (zero-latency) but we cannot push changes to all customers. We prioritize availability and minimal customer effort over micro-latency.

Streaming and rerank interactions: for rerank flows that use streaming and function/tool-calling (e.g., callers that stream candidate scores and then invoke tool calls), adapter must preserve chunked transfer-encoding and not buffer streaming responses end-to-end. We will implement a pass-through mode for streaming rerank traffic while still translating control-plane metadata (cursor and error trailers) inline.

Rollout plan: implement feature-flagged adapter (feature flag: compat.embedding.adapter). Canary to 5% traffic for 48 hours, observe error metrics and latency. Expand to 25% for 72 hours, then 100% if no regressions. If a spike occurs, auto-roll back to previous stable gateway.

Monitoring and observability: add per-cursor-mapping histogram, adapter error-rate metric (by mapping rule), and a trace tag 'compat_adapter_v1' so SRE can filter traces. Add synthetic iterator tests to production cron to validate cursor stability nightly.
qa_and_testing: Automated: unit tests for token translation, integration tests against a mocked vector store that simulates deletes/tombstones, fuzz tests for cursor corruption, and end-to-end compatibility tests using 3 legacy SDK versions. Manual: run canary with a small set of enterprise customers who agreed to opt-in. Test plan link: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/PM-756411-compat-adapter-testplan (internal).
migration_guide_and_docs: We will publish a migration playbook for customers. Key points: how to opt-in/out of adapter, what headers to expect (X-Legacy-Cursor, X-Compat-Errors), behavior for tombstones and partial results, and recommended client-side fallbacks. Docs draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Adapter+Backcompat
rollout_and_risk_mitigation: Feature flag on by default for traffic routed as 'legacy-sdk' user-agent. For unknown clients we will sample traffic to detect compatibility issues before enabling. Provide immediate fallback path: adapter will include an 'X-Fallback-Allowed' header; when set client can request 302 to the legacy gateway. Postmortem checklist and runbook created and linked in PR template.
